body.statement:
In Li and Zhao's unit-level finite-population setup, adaptive randomization permits treatment probabilities \(e_t(z)\) that are prespecified functions of the available history \(H_t\), are strictly between zero and one, and sum to one over treatment levels; potential outcomes are fixed under assignment randomness, and the adaptive AIPW regression at time \(t\) is constructed using only \(H_t\). Their AIPW Gaussian conclusion in Theorem 4(ii) requires Condition 3, whose part (ii), in their notation, is
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(V_{\mathrm{aipw}})^{-1}T^{-1}
 \max_{1\le t\le T}\frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}=o(1),
\]
where \(V_{\mathrm{aipw}}\) is the scaled AIPW covariance, \(\underline e_t\) is the smallest assignment probability at time \(t\), and \(L_t\) and \(M_t\) are the outcome and regression envelopes.

source.locator: arXiv:2602.21998v1, Definition 1, Sections 2.2--2.3, Condition 3(ii), and Theorem 4(ii)
source.verbatim_statement: Definition 1: $e_t(z)=\Pr(Z_t=z\mid H_t)$ is a prespecified function of $H_t$ satisfying $\sum_z e_t(z)=1$ and $e_t(z)\in(0,1)$. The design-based framework views covariates and potential outcomes as fixed and treatment assignments as the sole randomness. The adaptive AIPW estimator $\hat m_t(z)$ uses only $H_t$. Condition 3(ii) is $\lambda_{\min}(V_{\mathrm{aipw}})^{-1}T^{-1}\max_t (L_t+M_t)^2/\underline e_t^2=o(1)$.
